# Hard Problem Registry

&nbsp;

**An Open Registry of Hard Problems in Science**

&nbsp;

**Each observing is here whole with fields' own words, its incoming side: a hard problem as scientific method poses it.** Same observings are resolving with its momentarying side, living and non-living existing things co-sequencing, prior, now and next, each resolving with its field's own next. **One learning with two sides.**

# The conditions prior

Where science has a method for problems, five conditions stand prior to its acting.

The statement holds across readings.

The terms have determinate reference.

The accounts hold their truth value while under test.

A procedure repeating returns the same outcome independently of what precedes it.

Nothing prior enters: what comes to the statement brings nothing of what it held before.

Replication requires the first, measurement the second, inference the third, replication the fourth. The fifth is a condition on what reaches a statement, and the first four stand on it: a statement stands across readings where nothing reaching it brings a prior reading.

Five fix what enters and how it executes. A problem adds a sixth, its own, fixing its outcome: its outcome preserves a relation over a range, each as the problem states it. This condition is a problem's and not a method's, and it stands with Conserving relation and Conserving reach of every entry.

Everything below follows from these and from nothing else.

---

# 1 What stands open, and what stands firm

This is an open registry: a set of entries over a set of problems it states, each with one same set of properties.

**Problems are open.** No entry holds a settling answer to its own statement, except where its record settles one and its entry holds that settling.

**Intake is open.** This registry turns nothing away. It enters each observing, and its collection grows as observings come.

**Properties and checks are open.** Anyone with fields' literature executes any property or check against that literature.

**Each line is open with its observing.** A property with a filling carries an observing or its problem as its field poses it, said as itself, and never its source; a claim not observed directly is an anticipated observing. A line carrying neither is a claim nothing reaches, and it is check C1's case.

Against these, one thing stands firm: properties themselves. Every entry has one same set of properties, with one same order, whatever its field. Uniform elements are what make two entries comparable, and comparability is what a registry is for. Its schema closes once, one place only, so that nothing else has to.

---

# 2 Hard problems in science

**Science's problems** are hypotheses. A hypothesis is an account with consequences following from it, under test together with specifications it has. Where a consequence fails, a test refutes its conjunction of account and specifications and identifies no member of it. Where a consequence holds true, nothing follows about its account, a rival account entailing that same consequence.

**Hard** is where testing goes on and returns no refutation: either no consequence separating accounts is derivable, or accounts entail one same set of consequences. Both are properties of a hypothesis together with what it has, and neither is a property of what a hypothesis is about.

**Progress** is what stands: an establishing, a measure, a proof, or an exclusion. It accumulates whether or not a problem settles, every approach that ends returning a result about itself.

**Persistence** is a remainder between what stands and a settling result.

Each entry is one problem's statement as its field poses it, with progress and persistence and a remainder between them visible. Each entry has one same set of properties, each filling with an observing or with its problem, never with its source.

---

# 3 Derivation

## 3.1 What a refutation identifies

A refutation falls on a conjunction of account and specifications. It identifies no member of it. A test therefore returns no indication of which specification falls, where a settling result requires one to fall.

## 3.2 Specification

A hypothesis has every specification a consequence derives from. A hypothesis with fewer entails no consequence.

A specification is universal under a name where it holds across everything a statement says under that name, and local where it holds to one statement.

Nothing identifies a specification as one to withdraw, and specifications stand as many as a field brings.

## 3.3 Repetition

A result replicates where one same procedure returns one same outcome independently of what precedes it. A test with its own history is not replicable, and no test reads what a prior test produces.

Accumulation stands as specifications. A result that stands becomes a specification of tests that follow. Inference reads specifications as a test opens and writes to none of them.

Where a problem is durable, specifications stand firm across tests running against them. Testing's measure is its count of hypotheses under test.

## 3.4 The two responses

Where a test returns no refutation, refinement or revision follows.

Refinement sharpens a statement, its accounts, or its instruments, within specifications standing.

Revision withdraws a specification, retains its accounts, and tests again. Inference licenses neither, refuting a conjunction and identifying no member.

Both operate on what specifications permit. Neither response reaches a settling result specifications do not permit.

---

# 4 What an entry has

An entry has two parts. Its properties are of a problem, and stand whether or not any work goes on with it. Its report is of work on it, and stands empty where no record has any.

Each carries its observing and its problem, never its source, or is empty.

## 4.1 The properties

**Conditions prior.** Five, standing within every entry. Every unreachability result derives from these together with specifications below.

**Statement.** A problem's form as its field poses it, with its own words. Variant formulations stand, with no ranking.

**The field's account of its hardness.** Where a field states, with its own words, what is hard about its own problem — before anyone proposes an account. A field's own words, or empty. No inference from its record's difficulty.

**Accounts.** What each account proposes to exist, on its own content, as strongly as its record has it. Their number is as the field poses them. No relation between accounts stands here. A statement about an effort's condition proposes no account.

**Specifications.** Each specification a statement has besides five, with a name it is universal under, or local. Their number stands against a count of consequences derivable.

**Specifications withdrawn.** Each specification a record shows a field giving up while keeping its accounts. No reason stands, a refutation identifying no member.

**Common requirement.** What accounts require alike, where a field states it.

**Conserving relation.** What an outcome has to preserve, as its problem states it: an ordering that does not cycle, a procedure that returns, a predicate that divides cases, a value standing prior to measurement.

**Conserving reach.** A range over which its problem requires a relation, as the problem states it: all profiles, all programs, all statements of a language, all cases.

**Reach.** What a statement quantifies over. What its instruments return values over. Where a field states a relation between these two — an equivalence, a limitation with a proof, an account of what a method does not deliver — that statement stands.

**Unreachability.** A result establishing that a conserving relation does not hold over its conserving reach. A result is about its conditions and stands whether or not anyone makes an attempt. What anyone attempts stands with Approaches.

**Persistence.** A settling result, as its field specifies it.

## 4.2 The report

**Approaches.** Each direction a field takes, with its present reach by the measures it uses, and its standing: a refutation; a limitation with a proof blocking it; equivalent by construction to a rival; answering an adjacent question by a method's own account; instruments disagreeing on their object; narrowing; open.

**Narrowing recorded.** Where a record has its reach narrowing, or its relation weakening, with results following. Each stands as its record states it.

**Progress.** What stands, with its measures.

**Own record.** Where a field makes a statement about a problem's own standing, in the field's own phrasing.

## 4.3 Register

Properties have present standing: it is proved that; no algorithm is known; the bound stands at; the parameter space is excluded below; the estimates disagree by measured amounts.

No person functioning as attribution, no source and no date. Eponyms that are technical vocabulary stand where that vocabulary puts them.

## 4.4 Statement rule

A precise statement has nothing its original statement together with its own specifications does not have.

Short verbatim phrases stand where an exact formulation is itself an entry's object — a thesis by name, a canonical question — with a mark as such.

## 4.5 What an entry leaves out

Priority and sequence. In contest wherever a record has them, and no standing rests on it. A source, a citation, a finder's name and a publishing year: an entry carries its observing and its problem, never its source.

Importance, difficulty, promise. No statement has these.

An account no one proposes.

Any property of a problem by comparison with another problem.
